findings.what: The per-round attribution in the new rounds:M4.7a entry is shifted one round late against the verdict files, for two of the four rounds. (a) 'Round 2: the segment count became an allocation size, measured raising OutOfMemoryError past recover's own throws IOException' is ROUND 1's finding: .harness/review/4f1aa573...test-reviewer.json carries it as a major ('MEASURED ... {BDLT, v1, kind 0, seq 5, count 0x7FFFFFFF}: java.lang.OutOfMemoryError ... CommitLog.recover dies with an unchecked OutOfMemoryError straight past its own throws IOException'), and 4f1aa573...reviewer.json carries the same thing as a minor at CommitDelta.java:198. The round-2 record (f55329ad) contains no such finding, and could not: its reviewer minor quotes the NEW Cursor.remaining() javadoc, i.e. the bound already existed in the round-2 tree. Only the entry's second clause (the count-bound fixture with remaining()==0) is actually round 2's. (b) 'Round 3: the same allocation defect one field over, in the RUN count, reachable from the v0 path ... bounding one of two while a comment claimed the class was closed' is ROUND 2's pair of minors verbatim: f55329ad...reviewer.json at Cursor.java:42 ('The new remaining() javadoc asserts the count-as-allocation-size hole is now closed ... The invariant does not hold: CommitDelta.readSegment still does new ArrayList<>(runCount)') and f55329ad...test-reviewer.json at CommitDelta.java:222 ('PRE-EXISTING and byte-identical to HEAD ... a v0 delta body with runCount 0x7FFFFFFF'). What round 3 (f5ddef62) actually found is not described at all: both roles found that the new run-count fixture pinned only the absurd magnitude 0x7FFFFFFF with no modest-overclaim companion, plus a minor that neither guard's NEGATIVE half is constrained. No consistent reading of the entry ('what round N found', 'what round N's tree still contained', 'what round N's tree fixed') makes all four clauses true at once -- under the fixed-in-round-N reading the Round 1 clause becomes the wrong one instead. Separately, 'EVERY ROUND FOUND A REAL DEFECT IN CODE' is contradicted three sentences later by 'Round 4: passed both roles clean, no findings', though that one is self-correcting on the same line.
findings.failure_scenario: .harness/ is gitignored (.gitignore:12), so this entry is the ONLY durable record of what the five rounds cost and bought. A later auditor asking rule 12's question -- were the extra rounds productive, or was this the M0.53 tail the entry distinguishes itself from? -- reads that the segment-count OOM went unfound until round 2 and the run-count one until round 3, and concludes the reviews converged more slowly than they did; worse, the round the entry describes as finding an allocation defect (3) actually found a fixture-tightness defect, so the 'THE FIXTURES WERE THE RECURRING WEAKNESS' conclusion two sentences on is supported by one fewer round than the record shows. The correction is one round of the same defect class the entry is arguing about, which is why this is minor rather than major: rule 11 says fixing it is permitted and usually wrong.

findings.what: The quotation of the wire-format-change skill is not verbatim and the elision is unmarked. The skill says: 'One commit changes the format, every reader, every writer, the fakes, the conformance suite, the golden files, and the ADR.' The entry drops 'the conformance suite,' with no ellipsis, and then asserts 'The diff is exactly that set and nothing else.' The dropped member is precisely the one the diff does not contain -- and the remaining claim is loose in the other direction too, since the diff also carries the research-doc revision banner, the backlog row and this baseline entry, none of which are in the quoted set. (The omission is defensible on the merits: the only conformance suites in the tree are BinStoreConformance / ConditionalWriteConformance / MultipartConformance in binstore-spi, which cover the store SPI and not the chain-entry format -- but that is an argument to make, not to elide.)
findings.failure_scenario: A reader checking the argued entry against the skill greps the quoted sentence and does not find it, or -- worse -- takes the quote as the skill's full list and omits the conformance suite the next time a store-SPI format changes, which is the case where it is the load-bearing member. Every other quotation in this file (M4.21's, M0.53's, and the backlog row's ADR-0028 quote) marks its elisions with '...' or '…'.
